headline: Taiwan stocks hold 40,000, but foreign selling doubles to NT$76.6B and futures shorts grow
summary: Holding 40,000 is a breather, not a bottom: foreign investors are selling faster. Nvidia's results lifted the AI supply chain, but foreign net selling doubled in a day and net futures shorts rose. The index has closed below its 200-day line 3 days in a row; 2 more with a flat line trigger the defense rule. The bear line at 39,858 is only 0.8% away. Keep regular investing on plan.

overview.lead: Taiwan held on by a thread, it did not stop falling: the index edged up, but foreign selling doubled and only the AI supply chain rose.
points: The TAIEX rose 0.26% and closed above 40,000.
The intraday range was 1,677 points; it briefly fell below 40,000.
Foreign investors sold NT$76.6B, double the prior day, a 3rd straight day of selling.
Electronics rose 0.88% and financials fell 3.22%: money moved from banks to AI suppliers.
TSMC (2330) closed at NT$2,175, up just NT$5; the heavyweights did not join the bounce.

focus.lead: None of the nine tracked names hit a new tier today; the two Taiwan funds only have NAVs to 11/17, before today's small gain.
points: 0050 rose 0.1% and is −19.2% from its peak.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) is −33.9% from its peak on the 11/17 NAV, still the deepest of the nine.
MediaTek (2454), a top-3 name in Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8), rose 2.6% today, which helps the next NAV.
Both Taiwan funds hold AVC (3017) in their top 10; it hit limit-up today.
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) fell 0.9% on 11/17; tier 5 is now 6.6% away.
AB American Growth (LU0683600562) fell 1.1% on 11/17 and slipped just below its 200-day line.

position.lead: No new tier was hit today; the closest is still QQQ tier 3, 1.7% away.
points: QQQ tier 3 at 645.71 is 1.7% away (11/17 close).
SPY tier 2 at 701.18 is 4.3% away.
AB American Growth tier 2 at 85.08 is 4.6% away (11/17 NAV).
AB International Technology tier 5 at 1,218.74 is 6.6% away (11/17 NAV).
0050 tier 5 at 81.55 is 13.3% away.
Allianz Taiwan Technology and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend have used every tier; further NAV drops trigger nothing new.

macro.lead: No new macro pressure; Taiwan's strain comes from foreign outflows and US chip controls.
points: The Taiwan dollar weakened past 33 in the afternoon, quoted at 33.006 at one point.
A new US Commerce rule makes firms in Southeast Asia and Brazil apply for licenses to get advanced chips.
The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.10% (11/17); rates added no new pressure.
The high-yield spread is 3.34% (11/16), far from the 5% alarm line.

sentiment.lead: Fear is still here, but not capitulation: foreigners are selling hard, while margin traders have already pulled back a lot.
points: The CNN Fear & Greed index is 24.7, extreme fear.
Margin debt fell 21% over 20 days (11/17); deleveraging continues.
Foreign net TAIEX futures shorts are 99,438 contracts, up rather than down after settlement.
Investment trusts bought NT$17.6B, the only institutional buyer today.
Only 20% of listed stocks are above their 200-day line; 111 hit new lows.

sectors.lead: Today the AI supply chain bounced and financials were sold: Nvidia's results and its supplier list lifted cooling and substrate names.
points: AVC rose 9.9% to limit-up and Accton (2345) gained 6.8%; cooling and networking led.
ASE Technology (3711) rose 5.4% after SPIL signed a multiyear capacity deal with Nvidia.
Kinsus (3189) rose 6.8%, named among Nvidia's expanded substrate partners.
The financials index fell 3.22% and CTBC Financial (2891) dropped 5.3% as big lenders were sold.
Electronic components are still down 34% in a month; the bounce is only a start.

taiwan.lead: Foreign investors really are leaving: the index held 40,000, but their selling doubled, futures shorts grew, and investment trusts bought alone.
points: Foreign investors sold NT$76.6B, about NT$156.7B over the week.
Their 20-day selling is about NT$1.14T, still short of this site's extreme-selling threshold.
Net TAIEX futures shorts are 99,438 contracts, up 4,833 over the week.
This month's TAIEX futures settled at 40,025, 170 points below spot.
TSMC's ADR (TSM) trades about 9% above the local shares; tonight's ADR move sets up tomorrow's open.

watch.lead: Tonight through tomorrow, watch three things: the FOMC minutes, Walmart's results, and whether Taiwan holds 39,858 for a second day.
points: The October FOMC minutes come out early 11/19 Taipei time; markets already price a December hike.
Walmart (WMT) reports before the US open on 11/19 ET, a read on US consumers.
US initial jobless claims are out on 11/19 ET.
The TAIEX bear line at 39,858 is only 0.8% away.
Two more closes below the 200-day line with a flat line would trigger the defense rule.

regime.lead: By the rules, Taiwan is still a pullback in an uptrend, not a turn to bear, but the lean is "pullback, with rising risk", and the defense rule is just 2 days away.
points: Trend: the TAIEX has closed below its 200-day line 3 days in a row, 3.1% under; the line is still rising.
Defense needs 5 closes below a flat line; 2 days are left.
Systemic lights: 2 on (US index below its 200-day line, Taiwan breadth collapse); credit, growth and financial conditions are fine.
Closest to turning on is the Taiwan dollar slump light: the currency is near 33, down 0.58 in a month.
Bottoming signals: Taiwan has 3 on (margin deleveraging, breadth washout, new lows surge); foreign selling is not yet extreme.
History: all 10 past declines that reached this level went past −20%, and 4 went past −30%.
Only 3 fell this fast; the sample is too small, so use it only as a reference.
What would change the view: a close below 39,858 meets the bear-market definition.
A 3rd systemic light would mean a possible bear turn; the Taiwan dollar light is the likeliest 3rd.

news.title: November TAIEX futures settle at 40,025; the December contract closes at 40,312
news.read: After settlement, foreign net futures shorts rose to 99,438 contracts instead of falling; the shorts rolled into December.

news.title: USD/TWD hits 33.006 in the afternoon as the Taiwan dollar breaks past 33 again
news.read: Outflow pressure persists; this site's Taiwan dollar slump light uses a one-month move and is not on yet, but it is the closest 3rd risk light for Taiwan.

news.title: US tightens AI chip export controls; firms in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil must apply for licenses
news.read: The rule targets transshipment and remote access, not a full ban, but Southeast Asian data-center demand may slow, another risk for the AI supply chain.

news.title: Jensen Huang fallout spreads; scholars say 2027 orders are largely set and the near-term hit is limited
news.read: Near-term orders hold; longer term, watch how Nvidia's new leaders bargain with Taiwan server makers. Huang faces a closed-door House hearing on 12/1.
